pages.excerpt: Independent writing on media, craft, and the cost of attention — read in 74 countries, funded entirely by its members.

pages.body:
Why this exists

The Quarry started in 2020 as a set of notes between four editors who had all just been made redundant in the same quarter. The notes were about process — how many edits a piece should get, what a correction ought to cost, whether anybody was reading past the fold. They were not meant to be published.

Six years later they are the entire publication. We write for the people who run small publications: the founders, the editors, the one-person newsletters that pay a mortgage. Everything here is reported from inside that work rather than about it from a distance.

What we publish

Four beats, in rough order of volume: essays on independent media, interviews with editors and founders, field notes from publications trying something specific, and craft pieces on the mechanics of editing and type.

  • Essays — arguments about how the industry works and who it works for.
  • Interviews — long, edited transcripts. The subject sees their quotes before we run.
  • Field notes — short dispatches, usually with numbers attached.
  • Craft — house style, editing passes, typography, the unglamorous half.
If a piece would be better as an email to one person, we send the email instead.

Editorial standards

Every piece gets three passes — structure, argument, line — and no piece ships on its first. Corrections run at the top of the affected post, dated, with the original wording intact. We do not take sponsored posts, affiliate links, or paid placements in the recommendations list.

💡
Some of the publications we cover have been clients of our writers. Where that is true, it is disclosed in the piece.

How it's funded

Members, entirely. Free members get the weekly essay and the full archive. Paid members get the interviews, the annual field report, and the knowledge that five writers are paid a rate they agreed to rather than accepted.

Get in touch

Pitches, corrections and complaints all go to the same address, and all get read: editors@thequarry.press. We answer pitches within two weeks or not at all — if you haven't heard, it's a no.

Cheaper than the conference I stopped going to, and considerably more useful. — Paid member since 2021

Questions

Can I switch between monthly and yearly?

Yes, at any time from your account page. Switching to yearly credits whatever is left of the current month against the annual price.

What happens if I cancel?

You keep access until the end of the period you paid for, then the account reverts to free membership. Nothing is deleted and you can resubscribe with the same email.

Is there a student or hardship rate?

Yes. Email the editors and say so — no documentation required, no questions asked. Roughly one in twelve members is on a reduced rate.

Do you offer group or newsroom subscriptions?

For teams of five or more, write to the editors and we'll set up a single invoice at a reduced per-seat rate.

Where does the money go?

Writer fees first, then hosting and email delivery. There is no office, no advertising spend, and no outside investment.
